context: The Workdir tab currently displays working directory management functionality with New Setup, Archive, Current Iteration Status, and File Viewer sections arranged vertically. The prompt requests restructuring this page to be more compact with a clear hierarchy: status information at the top, buttons/actions in the middle, and file content at the bottom.

questions.question-text: How should the 'Current Iteration Status' information be displayed in the compact header?

options.label: Single horizontal row with key status fields (iteration-id, name, total prompts, next prompt ID) displayed inline with separators
options.pros: Most compact layout, all status visible at a glance without scrolling, efficient use of horizontal space
options.cons: May be cramped on smaller screens, less readable with long iteration names

options.label: Two-row layout with iteration info on first row and prompt statistics on second row
options.pros: Balanced between compactness and readability, groups related information logically, works better on medium screens
options.cons: Takes slightly more vertical space than single row option

options.label: Badge-style compact indicators for each status field arranged horizontally
options.pros: Clean modern look, color-coded status badges provide visual distinction, very compact
options.cons: May require abbreviations for field labels, less familiar pattern for status display

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option A provides the most compact layout while still displaying all necessary status information. Since the Web UI is optimized for desktop usage per requirement UR-20251224-0935, horizontal space is not a constraint, making a single-row layout ideal for maximizing vertical space.

questions.question-text: Should the New Setup and Archive buttons be combined into a single 'Actions' section or kept in separate cards?

options.label: Combine into a single horizontal 'Actions' section with buttons side-by-side
options.pros: More compact, reduces number of card containers, simpler visual hierarchy, faster to scan
options.cons: Less visual separation between creation and destructive operations

options.label: Keep separate cards but make them smaller and arrange side-by-side horizontally
options.pros: Maintains clear separation of concerns, card borders provide visual grouping, easier to add labels/descriptions
options.cons: Takes more space than fully combined option, more visual complexity

options.label: Use a button group with dropdown for less-frequently-used operations
options.pros: Extremely compact, hides complexity for advanced operations, clean primary action focus
options.cons: Reduced discoverability of archive function, requires extra click for some operations

questions.recommendation-rationale: Combining the actions into a single section aligns with the goal of making the page compact while maintaining clarity. Both New Setup and Archive are primary workdir operations that should be easily accessible, making option A the best balance of compactness and usability.

questions.question-text: How should the File Viewer section be structured to minimize space when not in use?

options.label: Show only Quick Access buttons by default, expand file editor on demand when a file is loaded
options.pros: Minimal space usage when idle, file content appears only when needed, matches current behavior, progressive disclosure pattern
options.cons: File editor collapses after saving which may be unexpected if user wants to make multiple edits

options.label: Use a collapsible accordion for the entire File Viewer section, collapsed by default
options.pros: Complete control over visibility, can hide entire section when not needed, standard Bootstrap pattern
options.cons: Requires extra click to access file viewer, may hide functionality from new users

options.label: Always show Quick Access buttons and a compact file path indicator, show full editor in a modal dialog when file is loaded
options.pros: Maximizes main page compactness, editor doesn't take up page real estate, can have larger editor in modal
options.cons: Modal dialogs feel heavier for file editing workflow, less fluid experience

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option A maintains the current progressive disclosure pattern where the file editor appears only when needed. This is the most compact approach while keeping the file editing workflow simple and inline, which is appropriate given that file editing is a secondary function in the Workdir tab.

user-selection.value: Add the buttons in the "Actions" section. Actions section should not have a title - it is clear what it is

questions.question-text: What visual styling should be used for the compact status header to make it visually distinct?

options.label: Light background panel with subtle border, similar to Bootstrap's alert-info style
options.pros: Clearly distinct from rest of content, familiar Bootstrap pattern, not too prominent, good readability
options.cons: Takes up some visual weight at top of page

options.label: No special container, just bold labels with values in the card body
options.pros: Most minimalist approach, no extra visual elements, maximum compactness
options.cons: Status info may blend with other content, less visual hierarchy

options.label: Dark header bar similar to card headers used elsewhere in the UI (bg-success style)
options.pros: Consistent with existing card header patterns, strong visual prominence, clear section delimiter
options.cons: Takes more visual weight, may be too prominent for status information

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option A provides clear visual distinction for the status information without being overly prominent. Using a light background panel creates a clear hierarchy where status is visible but doesn't dominate the page, aligning with the goal of a compact layout.

questions.question-text: Should the Quick Access buttons (Registry, Requirements, Technical Design) remain visible when a file is loaded, or should they be hidden?

options.label: Keep Quick Access buttons always visible even when file editor is shown
options.pros: Easy to switch between different files without closing editor, better workflow for reviewing multiple files, consistent UI state
options.cons: Takes up space even when not needed, slight visual clutter when editing files

options.label: Hide Quick Access buttons when file editor is displayed, show a 'Close' button instead to return to buttons
options.pros: More compact when editing, focuses attention on file content, clearer state transition
options.cons: Requires closing current file to switch to another, extra clicks for multi-file workflows, less efficient

options.label: Integrate Quick Access buttons into the file editor header area when a file is loaded
options.pros: Saves vertical space by combining navigation with editor, keeps access to file switching, compact layout
options.cons: More complex layout, header area becomes crowded, may be confusing which file is active

questions.recommendation-rationale: Keeping the Quick Access buttons always visible provides the best user experience for file navigation. Since these are small buttons, the space cost is minimal, and the benefit of easy file switching is significant for common workflows like comparing requirements with technical design.
